index.name: SUBSTRATE
index.question: How loaded is the physical substrate the models are being built on?

level_gloss: Ordinary. This is where most observations sit.

levels.name: SLACK
levels.gloss: The substrate is reading at the quiet end of its own record.

levels.name: STEADY
levels.gloss: Ordinary. This is where most observations sit.

levels.name: LOADED
levels.gloss: Above the middle of the record on more than one pillar.

levels.name: STRAINED
levels.gloss: Near the top of what this index has observed.

levels.name: MAXIMAL
levels.gloss: At the top of the record. A statement about our sample, not about the world.

pillars.name: The grid
pillars.blurb: How much load never switches off, and how little slack is left over it.

pillars.name: The water
pillars.blurb: The state of the rivers and the ground the clusters were built beside.

pillars.name: The build-out
pillars.blurb: What companies had to write down, and what the government had to publish.

sources.label: CAISO overnight floor
sources.direction: higher = more load that never switches off
sources.baseline_note: 14 of 30 points needed before this source can be scored

meta.source_note: CAISO publishes the current Pacific day only and carries no offset in the file; the calendar day is derived from the run clock and observed_at is the run instant

sources.label: ERCOT overnight floor
sources.direction: higher = more load that never switches off
sources.baseline_note: 15 of 30 points needed before this source can be scored

meta.source_note: net generation summed across all fuel categories, five-minute resolution; Power Storage is negative while batteries charge and that sign is kept

sources.label: ERCOT headroom used
sources.direction: higher = less slack between load and the committed fleet
sources.baseline_note: 14 of 30 points needed before this source can be scored

prc.ercot_note: There is enough power for current demand.

meta.source_note: capacity is COMMITTED capacity, which follows expected load, so this ratio understates the swing in physical margin; PRC is enrichment and never scored; rows ERCOT flags as forecast, and any row stamped after the run clock, are dropped before the ratio and the day high and low are computed

sources.label: NYISO overnight floor
sources.direction: higher = more load that never switches off
sources.baseline_note: 15 of 30 points needed before this source can be scored

meta.source_note: statewide sum of all eleven NYISO load zones; a timestamp missing any zone is discarded rather than summed short

sources.label: Severe drought, ten cluster states
sources.direction: higher = more of the build-out sitting in severe drought
sources.baseline_source: the same ten-state mean recomputed for every earlier week in the window
sources.baseline_note: 5 years of weekly maps; the current week is excluded

states.name: California
states.cluster: Santa Clara, the CAISO control region

meta.threshold: D2 — severe drought or worse; cumulative, so D2 includes D3 and D4
meta.source_note: US Drought Monitor, produced weekly by NDMC, USDA and NOAA; an expert assessment, not an instrument reading, and averaged here without area or population weighting

sources.label: Streamflow below normal, nine clusters
sources.direction: higher = less water in the rivers these clusters draw on
sources.baseline_source: the same nine-gauge median recomputed for every earlier day in the window
sources.baseline_note: 3 years of USGS daily values; the current reading is excluded

gauges.name: Trinity Rv at Dallas
gauges.note: ERCOT North; the densest Texas cluster

gauges.name: Goose Creek near Leesburg
gauges.note: Data Center Alley itself; a small local stream

gauges.name: Potomac Rv at Little Falls
gauges.note: the regional supply gauge for the DC metro

gauges.name: Scioto Rv at Columbus
gauges.note: New Albany and the Columbus corridor

gauges.name: Colorado Rv at Lees Ferry
gauges.note: the accounting point for Lower Basin deliveries, which is how Central Arizona Project water reaches Phoenix; it is 300 miles upstream of the datacentres and is a supply gauge, not a local one

gauges.name: Columbia Rv at The Dalles
gauges.note: the Oregon cluster sits on this river

meta.aggregator: median across gauges; the mean is reported but never scored
meta.lag_note: USGS daily values settle the following morning, so this reads one day behind
meta.source_note: denominator is the USGS published median for that gauge on that day of the year, over the gauge’s full period of record; it is not computed by this project

sources.label: Federal Register documents saying "data center"
sources.cadence: daily, on the federal publication calendar
sources.direction: higher = more federal paperwork touching datacentres
sources.baseline_source: the same 180-day rolling count taken at weekly anchors across the fetched corpus
sources.baseline_note: windows overlap, so these points are strongly autocorrelated and the effective sample size is much smaller than the count

meta.direction: higher = more federal documents mention datacentres
meta.source_note: the noisiest source in this index: "data center" also matches the National Climatic Data Center, federal facility consolidation notices and every agency building with the words in its name
